newsitem.title: CANADA: TimberWest expects news on fate in a week.
newsitem.headline: TimberWest expects news on fate in a week.

text.p: TimberWest Forest Ltd, which has put itself up for sale, said on Friday it hoped to make an announcement in about a week on its plans.

The lumber producer originally expected an announcement in late December but later pushed that to mid-January. Stephen Bellringer, a TimberWest director who is overseeing the process, said today that discussions were ongoing.

"We hope in the next week to 10 days to make an announcement," he said in an interview. The company was negotiating with bidders who submitted offers in December and exploring financial restructuring moves, he said.

The process has taken longer than expected because the directors sought studies that would compare the potential returns from equity alternatives to those from the sale of the company or some of its assets, he said.
Forestry firm Canfor Corp was considered by analysts to be the likely winner of the bidding with an offer rumored to be at least C$21 a share or C$643 million.
But the delay in announcing a deal and TimberWest's subsequent move to explore restructuring options have led analysts to speculate that Canfor's chances had diminished.

TimberWest and 52 percent-owner Fletcher Challenge Canada Ltd said in October they were putting TimberWest up for sale because they felt its stock was undervalued. Fletcher, majority-owned by New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Ltd, also expressed a desire to focus more intently on its paper business.

TimberWest has five lumber mills with annual capacity of 685 million board feet and its prize asset is 210,000 hectares of private timberland. That forest along with government timber tenures provides an annual harvest of 4.2 million cubic meters of wood.
